c_claim.say: Dustwell wants water. That's all it ever wanted. Light the core and Halloran says the leak into the aquifer seals itself. Kill the core and we limp along on the purifier chip, if we ever get it back. Either way, the town doesn't sell it and doesn't ration it.

opts.t: And if Haven 12 gets the regulator instead?

c_haven.say: Then four hundred people live who'd otherwise die, and Dustwell drinks green water for another ten years. I'm not going to tell you that's the wrong trade. I'm going to tell you I'd make the other one.

consequent.value: Even Kess

alternate.value: Everyone

value.cooked: has had a turn. Who gets the core?

opts.t: Saltreach. Ines's way: measured shares, nobody owns it.
The Lamplighters. Ro lights it, the whole valley gets it.
Kess. She's the only one who can hold it.
Nobody. I'll decide in front of the core.

c_done.say: All right. I'll pass it round. Wear this. It's tin, and it means you said it out loud in front of me. Out here, that's most of what a promise is.

c_kess.say: Kess. ...I asked, and you answered. Keep the star. I'd rather know where you stand than guess. Don't come to my town expecting to be bought a drink.

c_none.say: Nobody. Smartest answer and the most dangerous one. Take the star anyway. When you're standing in that chamber, remember everybody you didn't choose is waiting outside it.

l_read.say: Let me see that. ...Pell Haskins. Mordecai at the well-house. My own cousin. Every one of them selling Kess our water by the barrel, and Kess writing it down so she'd know who to squeeze. Where did you get this?

opts.t: Sable took me to it. She used to run with Kess.

l_done.say: Then thank her for me, and tell her the town owes her one, which is a sentence I never expected to say about one of Kess's people. I'll handle my cousin myself.

i_claim.say: Saltreach doesn't want the core. We want what comes out of it. A lit core seals the leak under the flats, and the deep aquifer is clean for everyone. Measured shares, written down, and a joint crew to run it. Nobody owns water. They only borrow it.

opts.t: And if it goes to Haven 12, or Kess?

i_else.say: Haven is a sealed box with a sad story. I don't blame them, but I won't pay for them either. Kess is a tax with a gun. If she gets it, Saltreach will be counting her cups instead of our salt.

oc_ines.say: Oskar. Oskar Vane, whose salt I have eaten at my own table. ...Thank you. And thank Renn, who I see is standing very straight. Saltreach will fine him every chit the Gulch ever paid him and he'll pan the flats by hand for a year. In public.

r_claim.say: You already know what I want. I woke it. My grandmother kept the manuals in her coat for fifty years so somebody could. Lit, it powers every pump from here to the salt. Cold, it's a tomb with a fence round it.

opts.t: People say you put the valley in danger.

r_risk.say: I did. The leak was already there; I made it loud enough that somebody would have to fix it. That's a crime, probably. So is letting a valley drink poison quietly.

k_claim.say: Here's my claim: I'm the only one who can hold it. Voss has six deputies. Ines has accountants. Ro has a church with no roof. I have the yard, the guns and the pumps. Bring me the regulator and the valley drinks every day. At a price. Everything has a price.

k_threat.say: Then someone else holds it and I take it off them. It'll just cost more, and you won't get a cut. Go on. Ask the others. I like being the last one you hear.

l_back.say: My ledger. Sable, of course; she always did like reading over my shoulder. Three hundred chits and we forget this happened. Where is she?

opts.t: Out of your reach. Here. Take it.

l_paid.say: Pleasure. If she comes back round, I'll know you sent her. Don't send her.

f_box.say: That's... that's my lead wagon's box. The maps. My mother drew half of these and her father drew the rest. Jory found it? Tell him the debt's paid. Tell him it was never his to pay. I'll put his name on the coastal sheet.

opts.t: He'll be glad to hear it.

v_maps.say: Pre-war survey sheets, oilcloth and all. People will pay to know where the old roads go. Four hundred chits, and the house never asks where things come from.

v_sold.say: A pleasure. If your bodyguard comes asking, I bought them off a stranger.

j_ask.say: Once. Two years back, western road past the chapel. Vulture Jack's crew came out of the scrub at dusk. I got two of them, they got the driver and the lead wagon. Finch never said a word about it. That's worse.

j_box.say: The strongbox. Finch's family maps, pre-war. Jack's lot couldn't open it and couldn't sell what they couldn't open. If it's anywhere, it's by the wreck. Some of his crew still camp out there.

j_go.say: Yeah? ...Yeah. All right. Western road, past the Burned Chapel, where the ditch runs black. I'll know it.

j_sold.say: You sold them. To Vex. I told you whose they were. ...I'm done. Pay me what you like; I won't be counting it.

consequent.value: Honestly? Best job I've had. You make me feel like the good guys still exist.
I'm watching you, boss. Don't give me a reason.

alternate.value: Feet hurt. Rifle's clean. That's a good day out here.

j_loyal.say: Trust you? ...I hired out for ten years and I never once turned my back on the person paying me. I turn it on you now and I don't think about it. That's new. Don't make me regret it. You won't. I know that.

j_refuse.say: We're done. I don't work for you, and I don't want your chits.

s_ask.say: Six years. I left because she started writing down people instead of crates. There's a ledger in her stash: every Dustwell fool who sold her water on the quiet. When the wells fail, she squeezes them first.

s_go.say: Now you're fun. Her stash is the locker by the crane, east side of the yard. Walk in like you belong there. Nobody looks at people who look bored.

s_burn.say: Give it here. ...You know what's nice about paper? It doesn't get a second opinion.

s_burned.say: There. Kess doesn't know who sold her out, Dustwell doesn't know who sold them out, and I sleep better. I owe you one. I don't say that.

consequent.value: Bored? With you? You walk into a room and something always catches fire. I love it.
You're turning into a saint, you know that? It's disgusting.

alternate.value: Fine. Hungry. Bit bored. Point me at something.

s_loyal.say: Bored? No. That's the strange part. Kess paid better and I never once wanted to stay. You don't ask me to be nice, you don't ask me to be sorry. You just keep walking into trouble and assuming I'll follow. I will. Don't tell anyone.

s_refuse.say: No. You had your chance to be interesting.

r_join.say: Ines would tell me to go. She'd also tell me to bring back whatever I borrow, so try not to get me shot. All right. Saltreach can spare one deputy.

r_refuse.say: No. I know what you are now. I used to be it.

consequent.value: Partner.

alternate.value: Need something?

opts.t: Coyle had a list on her.

consequent.value: Better than I have any right to be. I wake up and nobody's looking for me. Except you, and you're asking how I am. Weird.
Honestly? You're starting to remind me of the Gulch. I'm not saying that to be cruel.

alternate.value: Sore feet. Clean conscience. Mostly clean. Getting there.

r_ask.say: A Gulch rider came through Saltreach last week. Coyle's people. Mags has put two hundred chits on the deserter, alive or otherwise. That's me. Her crew's sitting in the dry wash under the Gulch, waiting for the salt wagons, and for me.

r_go.say: I was hoping you'd say that. I was also hoping you wouldn't. Dry wash, south-east of the Gulch. Coyle wears a red scarf. She'll want to talk first. Don't let her.

r_list.say: Let me see. ...That's the wagon schedule for the whole month. And that hand, all loops and no blots, that's Oskar Vane's. He's been selling his own town's routes to the Gulch. Probably so the other salt companies get hit and his crust goes up in price.

opts.t: Let's have a word with Oskar first.

r_ines.say: Good. Ines will want to read it twice and then shout once. I'll stand behind you. It's my town now. Funny how fast that happens.

r_oskar.say: All right. But if he offers you money, I'm going to be standing right there, and I'm going to remember what you say.

r_loyal.say: Have I? ...Yeah. In the Gulch you learn that everybody's a price. Then you walked out of nowhere and treated me like I was a person who could be trusted with a rifle. So. Whatever you need, wherever. That's not a deputy talking. That's me. Here, take the spare badge.

oc_face.say: Ah. That's my handwriting. ...Before you say anything: the Gulch was going to hit someone's wagons. I made sure it wasn't mine. That's not a crime, that's business. Here, two hundred and fifty chits, and you lose that list in the salt pan.

arguments.value: He watched you take the money

opts.t: People died on those wagons. You're going to pay their families. Today.

oc_bribed.say: Sensible. You'd be surprised how rarely I meet someone sensible. Your friend with the badge is giving me a look, by the way.

oc_pays.say: ...Fine. Fine! The families. Out of my own pocket. You've a nasty way of being right. Don't tell Ines. Please. I'll pay double if you don't tell Ines.

i_loop.say: A coolant bypass loop? ...You know, that would buy the old regulator a week, maybe ten days, if nobody breathes on it. It won't save us. It'll give you more time to find the part. Hand me that spanner. And go, before I start liking you.

i_metal.say: Heavy metals? From the pipes? ...Grey gums, tremor, the ringing ears. You're right, and I've been treating half of Dustwell for the wrong thing. Here. Take these for your trouble, and I'll start boiling the town's water through charcoal.

arguments.value: Spotted the lead in the water

i_ant.say: Impedance mismatch. Of course it is. I've been shouting into a pillow for a month. ...Look at that: half the noise gone. You want a job? No? Then take these, I've got spares, and I owe you a song.

consequent.value: Anything on the road?

alternate.value: Mayor's office. Such as it is. What do you need?
You came through Kettle Pass? On foot? Then you're either brave, lost or selling something. I'm Odile Brandt. I run Cinder Gap, which mostly means I count the water and listen to people shout.

opts.t: You look like you've got a problem.
I found Hester Vail. She's alive, and she told me who sent her.
Who else should I know around here?

town.say: Forty-one people, one deep well, and the only road through the Ashwood that doesn't go uphill both ways. Caravans come in from Mercy, the Kettle, the Ashborn when they feel like trading. We feed them, water them, fix their axles and take a cut. That's the whole economy. It works when the caravans arrive.

problem.say: Three caravans down the Mercy road this season. None back. Not a wheel, not a mule, not a drover come limping in. The Kings at the old drive-in tax anything that passes, but they've never kept a whole train before. I need someone who isn't from here to go and look. Someone the Kings won't recognise.

pay.say: Three hundred chits from the town chest, which is about a third of the town chest. And the Gap will remember your name kindly, which out here is worth more than you'd think.

opts.t: Make it four hundred. Three caravans is a lot of trade.

pay_more.say: ...Four hundred. If you bring back the wagons, or what happened to them. Don't tell Pike I said yes that fast.

yes.say: The last train left eleven days ago: four wagons, Hester Vail driving the lead. Hester's careful. If she wrote anything down, it'll be in her trail book. Start on the road south-east, past the canyon ford.

consequent.value: South-east road, past the ford. If you find wreckage, look for Hester's trail book.
The Kings. Of course. Marquee holds court in front of that screen like it's still showing something. I don't care how you settle it, as long as the road opens.

alternate.value: Mercy Falls? Why would they... No. Go on. Tell me when you know.

opts.t: One more thing about the last caravan.

secret.say: Hester's log says "per O.B." Those are my initials, yes. I... the town council voted against sending anyone to Mercy. Ghouls, they said. But Doc's running out of medicine and the pharmacy's right there. So I asked Hester, quietly. If she's dead, that's on me.

opts.t: You didn't lose three caravans to Mercy. Only the last one went there.

secret2.say: Right. The first two were the Kings, and I paid for that silence too. A mayor who loses caravans gets voted out; a mayor who loses them to bandits gets sympathy. ...You're going to do what you want with that. I know.

end.say: Alive. Thank God. And she told you, of course she did. So. Do I stand up in the Ember Room and tell forty people I sent their cousins into a ghoul nest behind their backs? Or do you let it lie, and I spend the next ten years making it up to them quietly?

opts.t: They deserve the truth. Tell them, or I will.
Let it lie. You meant well and Hester's home.
Tell them yourself, and tell them why. They'll forgive the reason.

arguments.value: Talked the mayor into the truth

end_told.say: Yes. Well. I'd rather it came from me. Here: the town chest's share, minus what I'll owe Hester. I expect I'll be "former mayor" by the end of the week.

consequent.value: Four hundred, and a bit over.

alternate.value: Four hundred, which is more than I promised.

value.cooked: Thank you. I won't forget it, and neither will the chest.
If anybody asks, the Kings took the wagons and you sorted the Kings.

end_both.say: I said it. All of it, in the Ember Room with the shutters open. Juno poured me a drink after and nobody threw it at me. They want me to stay. God knows why. Thank you.

opts.t: They know you'll tell them now. That's why.

people.say: Pike runs the store and thinks he runs the town. Juno keeps the Ember Room and knows everything said in it. Doc Sorrel is the only medic between here and the Kettle. Abe Kinney fixes anything with a bolt in it. And east, in the hills, the Ashborn. Be polite to them. They remember.

ashborn.say: A tribe. Came out of the forest fires when I was a girl and decided the fire had chosen them. They trade fair and fight hard. Lately their Ember-Speaker's been preaching against "the tower", which I assume means old Crane at the lookout. Crane's harmless. Mostly.

consequent.value: Back again. Wallet first, conversation after.

alternate.value: Pike's Goods. Everything from the Kettle to Mercy, at prices that are fair if you've never been anywhere else. I'm Pike. I also sit on the council, so be nice.

opts.t: What's the word on the road?
You'd pay for medicine, wouldn't you?
What do you think of the mayor?

word.say: Word is the Mercy road's cursed, the Kings are getting greedy, and the Ashborn are sharpening things. Also, a caravan from the Kettle says the valley's got a new hero who walked out of a vault. You wouldn't know anything about that.

hero.say: Ha. Then you're bad for business: people who walk out of vaults buy one of everything. Go on, make me rich.

mayor.say: Odile? Honest as a brick and about as flexible. She's been odd this season. Counting the chest twice. Asking Doc how long the medicine lasts. If you're working for her, ask her where the last caravan was really going.

mayor2.say: I know the last train loaded empty crates and water for a week, which is more water than you need for a three-day run to Mercy and back. I keep the books. Books notice.

meds.say: A full case? Sealed? Five hundred chits, right now, cash. Doc will tell you it's for the sick. I'll tell you the sick will pay me for it either way, and you'll be five hundred richer.

arguments.value: Sold the town's medicine to Pike

opts.t: No. It goes to the Doc.

meds_sold.say: Pleasure. Doc's prices will be very reasonable, considering.

consequent.value: He's here. He's really here. Talk to me before I start crying into the till.
What'll it be?

alternate.value: Welcome to the Ember Room. It was the Mercy Falls Feed and Grain once; the sign's better now. I'm Juno. First drink is half price if you tell me something I don't know.

opts.t: I'll have a look at what you're pouring.
You look like something's eating at you.
I'm sorry, Juno. Dex didn't make it.

elements.value: The Ashborn's Ember-Speaker came to trade last month and wouldn't drink. Said the fire drinks for him. I've met that type. It's never the fire.
Abe Kinney rebuilt a whole Corvega engine from two dead ones and a lawnmower. Doesn't drive. Just likes knowing it would.
Crane, the old man in the fire tower, used to come in once a season for coffee and gossip. Hasn't for a year. Somebody should check he's breathing.
There's a light at night up at Mercy General. Ghouls don't need lights.

dex.say: My brother. Dex. Nineteen, all elbows, thinks he's immortal. He ran off to the Reel Kings at the drive-in three weeks ago because Marquee gave him a jacket and called him "kid". If somebody clears the Kings out, he'll be in the middle of it. Would you... could you talk to him?

dex_yes.say: Tell him... tell him Mum's ring is still on the shelf behind the bar, and if he wants it he has to come and get it himself. He'll know what that means.

dex_home.say: He walked in, sat down at that stool, and asked for the ring. Then he asked for a job. I gave him both. I don't have much, but here. And drinks are on the house. Forever. Within reason.

dex_dead.say: ...Right. Right. Thank you for telling me yourself. Leave me alone for a bit, would you?

hub.say: Juno's got me washing glasses. Honestly? It's better than watching the screen with Marquee waiting for a movie that's never coming. Thanks for, you know. Talking sense.

consequent.value: Sick, shot or curious?

alternate.value: Sorrel. Doctor, by courtesy. I learned from a book and a man who learned from a book. Sit down if you're bleeding; stand up if you're not.

opts.t: I found the Mercy General pharmacy stock.
What do you know about Mercy Falls?

consequent.value: Forty chits and you'll walk out lighter by a few holes. ...There. Don't do that again.

alternate.value: Forty chits, and you don't have forty chits. Come back when you do, or when you're dying, whichever comes first.

meds.say: Short? I'm boiling bandages. Three fevers in the back and I'm treating them with willow bark and optimism. The pharmacy at Mercy General was the best in the county. The ghouls don't take pills. If you went...

meds_yes.say: East wing, behind the main hall. Look for the steel cage. And take this: if you breathe what's in there long enough, you'll want it.

meds_back.say: A whole case. Sealed. You... I'm going to sit down. That's three people who see next month. More. Here, everything in the tin, and if you're ever shot within a day's walk, crawl here.

mercy.say: It was a mill town with a waterfall, before the war took the river. The hospital served the whole valley. When the bombs fell people went there to be saved, and stayed, and... changed. Most of the ghouls up there were patients. Some of them were my teacher's teacher.

consequent.value: What's broken?

alternate.value: Abe Kinney. If it has bolts, I can fix it. If it has feelings, try Juno. You want a bench, there's one right there. Mind the oil.

me.say: Came up the Mercy road as a boy on the back of a mule. My father fixed wagons. I fix wagons, generators, guns, the water tower pump twice a month and Pike's till when he kicks it. Mostly I fix things people say can't be fixed, because I like the look on their faces.

radio.say: Crane's? The forestry set? Hand-crank, longwave. I rebuilt the crank on it six years back. Ashborn think it talks to the fire. It talks to nobody: there's nobody left on that band. He just reads out the weather to the dark. Makes him feel useful. Don't we all.

consequent.value: Road's open, they say. First quiet week we've had in a year.

alternate.value: Weapons stay holstered in town. Fights go outside the wall. Trade goes to Pike. Questions go to the mayor.

out.say: West, the pass back to the Kettle. South-east, the Mercy road: the Kings sit on it at the drive-in turn. North-east, the Ashwood, the lookout, and past that the Ashborn. Don't pick fruit in the Ashwood. Don't ask why.

hub.say: Name's not important. Your business is. Keep it peaceful.

consequent.value: It's quiet. Is it... is it actually quiet? Then I'm walking out of here and I'm not stopping till I see the water tower.

alternate.value: Still hear them in the hall. Clear them out and I'll run for it. I'm not brave, I'm just stubborn.
Don't shoot! Don't... you're not one of them. You're talking. Oh, thank God. Hester. Hester Vail. Did Odile send you? She must have. Nobody else knew we were here.

opts.t: Go. It's clear. Cinder Gap is waiting for you.
Hang on. I'll clear the way.

what.say: Odile asked me quiet: take the empty wagons to Mercy, load what's in the pharmacy, nobody needs to know. We got in fine. Then the ones in the wards woke up. The drovers ran. I locked myself in the cage with the pills and the water. Eleven days. I've been talking to the shelves.

drovers.say: Two made it to the trees, I think. Two didn't. ...The mules are all dead. Don't tell Pike, he'll want to bill me.

go.say: I'm going. Tell Odile... no, I'll tell her myself. Take what's left in here; I've marked the good shelves.

consequent.value: Odile told them. Took guts. I'm driving the Mercy run again come spring, with six guns this time and nobody's secrets.

alternate.value: Odile and I have an understanding. I don't talk about Mercy, she pays me to not drive to Mercy. Seems fair.
Eleven days in a cage and I'm alive because you can shoot. I owe you a lifetime of free axle grease. Go and see the mayor.

consequent.value: You again. Pull up a stump. The kettle's on, the forest's not, and that's a good day.

alternate.value: Well, now. A visitor. Sit, sit. Ellis Crane, Forest Service, Ashwood District, retired by nobody, still on duty. The tower's mine and so is the view. You're welcome to both.

opts.t: The Ashborn call you the Burning Man.
Can I see your fire log?
Give me the radio, old man.

service.say: Eleven years before the war and forty-odd after. Nobody told me to stop, so I didn't. I watch for smoke. When I see it, I take a bearing, I fire a flare over whoever's in the way, and I read the weather out on the radio in case anybody's listening. Nobody is. That's not the point.

point.say: The point is somebody's doing it. A forest wants a lookout. A lookout wants a forest. We keep each other company.

burning.say: Do they. ...Well. I suppose from the camp all they see is the flares going up and then the fire coming after. Cause and effect, to a child. I'm not the cause, friend. I'm the warning. Twice I've fired over their camp an hour ahead of the burn. It's in my log.

tull.say: Tull. Yes, I've met him. Came up the hill last spring, stood under the tower and shouted at it. Funny thing: both fires that hit their camp started on the east side, upwind, right where nothing burns on its own. Pines don't light themselves in the spring rain.

arson.say: I think if you went and looked under that big burnt pine they hang their charms on, you might find something that smells of lamp oil. I can't go. They'd skin me. You, they might only shout at.

log.say: Take it. Every smoke for eleven years, every bearing. If it keeps an old man's neck unstretched, it's done more good than most books. Bring it back when they're done arguing over it.

threat.say: The radio. Ah. You're that kind of visitor. ...No. It's the only voice I've got. If you want it, you'll have to take it off a dead man, and I'm slower than I was but I'm not dead yet.

threat_win.say: Fine. Fine! Take it. Take the voice off a man and see what the forest says to you after. Get off my hill.

consequent.value: The fire watches you kindly, outsider. Sit by it when you want.

alternate.value: Speak. The fire is listening, and so am I.
You walked through our gate without a spear in your back. Either my wardens have gone soft or the fire likes you. I am Saba. I speak for the Ashborn, when they let me.

opts.t: Can I trade with your people?

who.say: When the great fire took the forest, my mother was nine. She walked out of it with seven children who were not hers and none who were. The fire took everything and gave us each other. So we keep it. We feed it, we learn from it, we do not let it go out. Some of us think it speaks.

speaks.say: I think it crackles. Tull thinks it speaks. Tull is the Ember-Speaker, so he would know, he says.

worry.say: Twice in five years the fire came for the camp instead of the forest. Both times, the night before, red stars rose over the tower in the hills. Tull says the man there, the Burning Man, calls the fire down with his voice-box. He wants my hunters to go up the hill. I would rather someone who is not angry went first.

worry_yes.say: Good. Go to the tower. Look at him. Then come back and tell me what you saw, not what you were told. Bring me something I can hold up in front of the fire.

opts.t: [Show the fire log] He's a fire warden. Both times, his flares warned you an hour before the fire came.
[Show the oil rags and flint] These were under the Ember Mother. With Tull's ochre.
[Hand over the radio] Here's the Burning Man's voice.

r_log.say: Red stars, and then fire... an hour apart. Every time. He was shouting at us to run, and we were too busy hating him to listen. ...I will go up the hill myself, with meat and an apology. Take this. It means the fire has decided not to eat you.

consequent.value: And he is already gone, I see. Good.

alternate.value: Tull! Come here and look at what the outsider found.

value.cooked: Tull's ochre. Lamp oil. Under the Mother herself. ...He made us afraid so we would need him to tell us what the fire wanted.

r_tull2.say: Now he is not the Ember-Speaker. If he goes quietly, he goes. If he does not... Wardens, watch him. And you, outsider: thank you. The camp will remember who looked under the Mother when nobody else dared.

r_radio.say: So small. It does not look like it could call anything. ...Tull will be pleased. I am less pleased, and I do not know why. Here, for your trouble.

trade.say: Ira trades for the camp. Furs, meat, the good mushrooms. She is the one by the racks, laughing at something. She is always laughing at something.

consequent.value: The voice is silenced. The fire will be quiet now. You did well, outsider. Better than our hunters.
You brought the old man's scribbles to the Elder and she believes them. She is old too. Go away.

alternate.value: Outsider. You stand close to the Ember Mother. Stand further.

opts.t: Why do you hate the man in the tower?
Fires don't start on the wet side of a camp in spring. Somebody lit them.

tower.say: He sits above us. He watches us. He fires red stars and the fire comes. Before he came the fire was ours, and it spoke through me. Now it listens to him. Bring me his voice-box and the fire will be ours again.

consequent.value: It says nothing to me any more.

alternate.value: It says the camp must stay apart. It says outsiders bring the burning. It says... it says many things, and it says them to me.

accuse.say: ...You have been listening to the old man. Leave this camp before I decide what the fire says about you.

opts.t: You did it so they'd need you. Leave quietly and nobody has to see the rags.

leave.say: You would... Hm. Better to be a living Speaker somewhere else than a dead liar here. Keep your rags. Tell Saba the fire sent me walking.

arguments.value: Tull pulls his hood up and walks out through the gate without looking back.

consequent.value: You came back! Want to trade or want to hear about the boar that nearly ate me?

alternate.value: Ha! An outsider who looks at the racks instead of the spears. I'm Ira. I trade for the camp, because I'm the only one who can count past "many".

opts.t: The boar that nearly ate you?
What do you think of Tull?

boar.say: Big as a wagon! Well, a small wagon. A wheelbarrow. It came out of the ferns and I went up a tree so fast I left my boots on the ground. It ate one boot. I traded the other to Pike as "boar-tested".

tull.say: He was nice, when we were small. Then he got the ochre and started hearing things. He goes out to the east side at night a lot. Says he's praying. I followed him once. He wasn't praying, he was digging.

dig.say: Under the Ember Mother. That's not allowed. I didn't tell anyone, because who would believe me over the Speaker? Maybe they'd believe you.

consequent.value: Friend of the fire. Pass.

alternate.value: Walk slowly. Keep your hands where the fire can see them.

hub.say: Outsiders trade with Ira. Outsiders speak with the Elder. Outsiders do not touch the Ember Mother.

consequent.value: My favourite customer. The road's open, the chits come in, and nobody has to watch the second feature.

alternate.value: Welcome, welcome, to the Sunset Drive-In! Tonight's feature, same as every night: nothing. Tickets are free. Leaving costs. I'm Marquee, and these are the Reel Kings. What brings you to the pictures?

opts.t: Cinder Gap's caravans. You took them.

why.say: Because once upon a time a thousand people sat right here, in the dark, all looking the same way, and nobody shot anybody. I find that inspiring. Also, the screen makes a hell of a wall.

caravans.say: Took? We taxed. Two trains, fair and square: the screen tax, payable in mules. The third paid in chits and went on its merry way to Mercy, which is its own funeral. Anyway. You want the road open? Everything's got a price.

opts.t: Here's my price: you pack up and leave the valley, today.
A dead road pays you nothing. Take a cut from the Gap instead: steady money, no shooting.

price.say: Three hundred chits now, and the Gap pays the screen tax every season after. Small, civilised, regular. Like a subscription.

toll.say: ...Steady money. No shooting. You know, I've been waiting for someone to say something sensible to me for six years. All right. Tell Odile the Kings will take a toll, a small one, and anything going to Mercy is waved through. Have a ticket.

paid.say: Lovely. Road's open. Enjoy the show.

scare.say: Leave the... ha. Ha. You mean it. You've got the eyes. All right, all right. Kings! Pack the projector. We're touring. Somewhere with fewer heroes.

arguments.value: The Reel Kings load what they own onto two carts and roll off south, Marquee waving from the back.

fight.say: Ah. A critic. Kings! House lights!

dex.say: The kid? He's got heart and no aim. I like him. He's by the snack bar, pretending he isn't homesick. Go on, talk to him. If he wants to go, he goes. The Kings aren't a prison. We're a cinema.

hub.say: You're not a King. Did Juno send you? She did. She always sends somebody.

why.say: Because Marquee says I'm going places. In Cinder Gap all I'm going is from the bar to the well and back. Here, at least, there's... I dunno. Jackets.

home.say: And do what, wash glasses? No. I'm a King now. ...What did she say? Exactly?

opts.t: That your mother's ring is behind the bar, and you have to come and get it yourself.
That the Kings are about to get cleared out, and she'd like to bury you old, not this week.
You're coming home. Walk or be carried.

ring.say: ...She kept it. She said she'd sell it if I ever left. She kept it. ...Okay. Okay. Tell Marquee I said thanks for the jacket. I'm keeping the jacket.

arguments.value: Dex shrugs his jacket straight and sets off up the road to Cinder Gap.

scared.say: Cleared... by you? Yeah. Yeah, you look like the clearing type. I'm going. I'm going! Tell Juno I was always going to.

drag.say: Ow! All right! I'm walking! You're worse than she is.

elements.value: Water's on at the tower after noon. Bring your own bucket.
You came over the pass? My uncle tried that once. Came back with no shoes and a lot of opinions.
Don't let Pike sell you the "boar-tested" boots.

consequent.value: Wagons are moving again. Feels like the whole town took a breath.

alternate.value: Three caravans gone. My sister drove the second one.

hub.say: Abe fixed my rifle with a spoon. I don't know how. I don't want to know how.

consequent.value: They say the Speaker lied to us. I knew his eyes were wrong.

alternate.value: The fire is fed. The camp is safe. Go and speak to the Elder.

hub.say: Outsider. Your boots are loud. The forest hears you coming a mile off.

consequent.value: Well? What's in my water?

alternate.value: Harbourmaster. What can I do for you?
Stranger. You came down from Northgate, which means you've walked a long way to look at a lake. I'm Nell Okafor. I keep the harbour, the water ledger and the peace, in roughly that order.

opts.t: You look like you've had bad news.

town.say: Before the war it was a reservoir for a city that doesn't exist any more. After, it was the only water for forty miles that didn't glow. We fish it, filter it and sell it south by the barrel. Half the canteens in the valley were filled here, whether they know it or not.

fish.say: Now the fish at the north end are coming up dead with green in their gills, and Mara's nets come up slick. If the south hears Stillwater water is going bad, we're finished long before the water is. I need someone who isn't a fisher to walk up to the inlet and look.

pay.say: Two hundred and fifty chits, a barrel of clean water a month for as long as there's a Stillwater, and my personal opinion of you, which is currently "probably fine".

yes.say: The inlet's at the north end, where the stream comes down off the hills. There's an old pipe up there nobody's ever followed. Take a jar.

consequent.value: North inlet. The stream and the old pipe. Bring me something I can show the council.

Silo 9? That's the bomb hole east of here, the one the pilgrims sit around. If anybody knows what a silo leaks, it's Tobiah Fenn. He used to fix our pumps. The Highrisers took him to their tower in Old Meridian last month and want a fortune for him.

alternate.value: So it's the silo. Then go and shut it. And come back, will you? We're short on people who come back.

consequent.value: The inlet's running clear. Mara caught a perch this morning that wasn't the colour of a traffic light. You did that. Stillwater won't forget it, and neither will I.
We felt it here. The whole lake shivered. The inlet's clearing, slow. Whatever was down there is under a lot of rock now. I hope you knew what you were doing.

alternate.value: The water's clearing. The pilgrims say the Bowl is glowing brighter than ever. I don't want to know what you traded for my fish, do I.

opts.t: Your water's safe. That's what matters.

consequent.value: Back for more fish? Everybody comes back for the fish.

alternate.value: Gus Pruitt, Stillwater Co-op. Water by the jug or the barrel, fish smoked or the other kind, and anything a fisher needs that isn't a better boat. Mara does boats.

consequent.value: Booming. Water's clean, fish are fat, and every caravan from the south wants three barrels. I've started charging extra for jugs with handles.

alternate.value: Quiet. Too quiet. I've stopped selling north-end fish and started selling "lake-style" jerky, which is jerky I've told a story about.

hub.say: Mind the hull, she's drying. Mara. I build the boats and mend the nets, and lately I pull dead fish out of them. What do you need?

opts.t: What have you seen out on the water?

seen.say: Green slick at the north end, mornings, like oil on a puddle. The gulls won't land on it. And at night, from the middle of the lake, you can see a glow over the hills to the east where the bomb hole is. It's brighter than it was last year.

boats.say: Flat-bottomed skiffs. Draw nothing, carry plenty, and they don't sink unless you ask them nicely. Sit in one sometime. It's the only quiet place left in the world.

hub.say: Stillwater. Drink what you buy, fish where you're told, and don't piss in the lake. Everybody's downstream of somebody.

consequent.value: The perch are back! Little ones, but back.

alternate.value: Nets came up empty at the north end again. Empty and green.

hub.say: Shh. They can hear you through the boards. ...No, I don't know if that's true. My grandad said it.

consequent.value: The pumps are humming and the inlet's running clear. I'm an old man fixing other people's pumps again. It's a good life. Thank you for it.

alternate.value: Nell's given me a room over the co-op and a pump to fix. If you're going down to Silo 9, the codes are in your head now. Don't let the Prophet near that console.

consequent.value: What do you need? Guns, bullets, or a reason to live? Only got the first two.

alternate.value: Welcome to the Garage, the only roof in Old Meridian that isn't charging rent to the Duchess. Velma Cruz. I sell what kills things and buy what's left over.

duchess.say: The Duchess runs the Highrisers out of the Spire, the tallest thing standing in the city. She thinks the skyline is hers because she can see all of it. Everybody pays her rent. We pay in bullets, which she respects more than chits.

tobiah.say: Tobiah Fenn. Our engineer. Built the generator that runs this place, keeps our water pump spinning, taught half the kids in here to read off old manuals. The Highrisers grabbed him on a parts run and the Duchess wants six hundred chits. I've got two.

yes.say: You're either brave or you haven't met her. The Spire's two blocks in, the tall one with the lobby lit. They let visitors in. Leaving is the trick.

consequent.value: and the Duchess is dead. The whole city heard. Nobody's going to miss her rent.

alternate.value: and nobody had to die for it. I owe you.

value.cooked: Here, from the Garage. Every one of us chipped in.

hub.say: Inside the barricade it's Garage rules: no shooting, no stealing, no Highrisers. Outside it's the city's rules, and the city doesn't have any.

consequent.value: Still here. Still in a cage. Still very much hoping you're working on that.

alternate.value: Oh, a face that isn't a Highriser's. Tobiah Fenn. Engineer, prisoner, enthusiast of fresh air. Did Velma send you?

opts.t: Stillwater's water is being poisoned. A pipe stamped SILO 9 COOLANT.

silo.say: Silo 9. God. When the warhead was safed they rigged a coolant purge so the core couldn't cook off: a pump that dumps the loop into the old drain line. Seventy years later, the drain line runs under the hills into your reservoir. Someone has to shut the purge from the launch console. You need a crew key or my override codes, and I'm not giving codes through bars.

opts.t: Then I'll get you out of the bars.
Where do I find a crew key?

key.say: The guard robot at the silo carries one. The pilgrims call it the Iron Angel and pray to it, which is a terrible idea, because it shoots people who pray too close.

out.say: Lovely. The Duchess has the only chain key, and she likes it more than she likes me. Of course, the padlock's pre-war and I could open it with a hairpin if anybody gave me one, which they haven't, because they're not idiots.

opts.t: I'll see what I can do.

consequent.value: The engineer's gone. I hope you enjoyed being clever. Pay your rent on the way out.

alternate.value: A tourist! Welcome to the Spire. Everything you can see from the roof is mine, including you, as of the moment you walked in. I'm the Duchess. What brings you to my lobby?

why.say: Because it's the tallest. When the world ended, everybody went down into holes. I went up. You can see a raider coming for an hour from up there, and you can see every fire in the city, and every fire is somebody I can charge.

fenn.say: The engineer! My best investment this year. Six hundred chits. Non-negotiable, except when it is.

opts.t: He's worth more to you grateful than ransomed. Let him fix your generator and pay him in fish.
Six hundred chits for one old man? I'll give you four, and you'll take it.
Let him go or I start renting your lobby out to the crows.

paid.say: Pleasure. Take him. Mind the stairs, they're mostly ornamental. And have a token; it means you've paid. For now.

talk.say: ...Fish. You want me to pay him in fish. ...My generator has been making that noise for three weeks. Fine. He goes, he comes back once a month and fixes my lights, and Stillwater sends me a barrel. You're a terrible influence.

haggle.say: Four. You've got eyes like a landlord. ...Four, then, and you never stand in my lobby looking at me like that again.

fight.say: Oh, I like you. Highrisers! Evict this one.

consequent.value: The Sleeper's breath is in the Bowl. Can you feel it? Warm. Warm as a hand.
You came back to the light. They always come back.

alternate.value: Welcome, pilgrim, to the edge of grace. Down there, under the glass, the Sleeper waits. The old world built it to end the world. It refused. It lay down instead. I am Sel, and I listen to it dream.

opts.t: What do you want from me?
Your people are dying, Sel. Amon wrote it all down.

sleeper.say: A warhead, the scoffers say. Safed and sleeping. But look at the glass, pilgrim. Look at the light in the pools. Something down there is breathing. When the silo is opened, its breath will fill the Bowl and we will be changed, the way the glass was changed. Made clean.

want.say: The Iron Angel guards the door and keeps the key. It will not let the faithful near. You are not faithful. It may let you near enough. Bring me the key and I will open the Sleeper's eye myself.

key.say: Oh... oh, pilgrim. Give it here. Tonight we walk down into the Bowl with lanterns, all of us, and I turn the Sleeper's eye to the sky. ...Thank you. You will be remembered as the one who carried grace.

arguments.value: Gave the Prophet the silo key
That night a line of lanterns winds down into the Glass Bowl. In the morning the pools are brighter, and the Stillwater inlet runs clear.

truth.say: Readings. Numbers. Amon has always loved numbers more than faith. ...Eleven names. I knew all of them. I... I told them it was grace.

opts.t: It wasn't. Take them out of the Bowl, Sel. Take them to Stillwater. Nell will feed them.

saved.say: ...Yes. Yes. The Sleeper never spoke. I spoke, and called it the Sleeper because no one would listen to Sel. We will go. Tomorrow, all of us. Will you tell the woman at the lake we're coming? We'll work. We know how to carry water.

arguments.value: Led the Children out of the Bowl

snap.say: Liar! Heretic! The Sleeper sees you! Wardens!

consequent.value: They're packing. All of them. Sel too. I've been trying to find a word for what I feel and the only one I've got is "lighter".
You gave him the key. ...I suppose I knew someone would. I'll stay. Somebody has to bury them.
The Prophet is dead. The others are lost without him, but they're alive, and lost can be fixed.

alternate.value: Keep your voice down. I am Amon. I believed, once. Then I found an old dosimeter in the silo's guard hut and I started counting. Will you hear me?

count.say: Eleven pilgrims in three months. Hair first, then gums, then they stop eating. Sel calls it "being changed". The dosimeter calls it four hundred rads. He wants the silo opened. If he opens it, there won't be anyone left to change. Talk to him. Then decide. You're the only one here who isn't afraid of him.

opts.t: Give me the log. I'll talk to him.

consequent.value: Thank you. Truly. Here, it's not much. The Children have never had much. That was rather the point.

alternate.value: It's done, then. Whatever comes, you looked at it with open eyes, which is more than most of us managed.

hub.say: Walk softly on the rim, pilgrim. The glass remembers every footstep.
Have you looked down into the Bowl at night? The pools shine like a city. Like the city must have looked.
My hair came out this morning. The Prophet says it means the Sleeper has noticed me.
Nell says I can mend nets. I've never mended anything. Everything's been breaking for so long.

consequent.value:
SILO 9 :: STANDBY
COOLANT PURGE ........ SEALED
CORE TEMPERATURE ...... NOMINAL
WARHEAD ............... SAFED
SILO 9 :: NO CARRIER

alternate.value:
SILO 9 :: STANDBY  (DAY 26,447)
COOLANT PURGE ........ ACTIVE  > DRAIN LINE 4
CORE TEMPERATURE ...... NOMINAL
WARHEAD ............... SAFED

TWO-MAN RULE IN EFFECT. ONE KEY DETECTED.

opts.t: Redirect the purge into the Bowl instead of the drain line.
Run the core past its limits and bury the silo.

shut.say:
PURGE VALVE 4 ........ CLOSED
LOOP PRESSURE ......... RISING
RECIRCULATION ......... ENGAGED

Somewhere under your feet, a pump that has run for seventy years stops.

vent.say:
PURGE ROUTED > SURFACE VENTS 1-4

Outside, the pools in the Bowl begin to bubble and glow brighter. The drain line under the hills runs dry.

blown.say:
CORE TEMPERATURE ...... 412%
CONTAINMENT ........... FAILING
SILO DOORS ............ SEALING

You have about four minutes to be somewhere else. The silo is going to fold itself into the earth.

arguments.value: The ground shudders as Silo 9 collapses into itself. A long breath of dust rolls out of the Bowl.

epilogue.t: You told Sheriff Voss the water was Dustwell's, and it was. She wore her own tin star to the purifier's first run and pinned it on the pump.
Ines Duarte wrote the shares on the wall of the Saltreach well-house in white paint. Your line says "one cup, for the one who kept their word."
The Lamplighters lit a lantern for every promise kept that year. There were not many. Yours hung highest.
The Overseer read your name aloud at the next ration count. Four hundred people stood up for it.
Kess paid you exactly what she promised, which was the only honest thing anyone in the valley expected of her.
You stood in Sheriff Voss's office and named a side, and then you chose another. People in the valley still repeat what you said. They say it the way you say a joke nobody laughs at.
You never told the council whose side you were on. Some called it wisdom. Most just remembered the tin star, and that you had worn it without ever saying a word.
Odalys Finch's coastal sheet came out the next spring. In the corner, in small careful letters: "Survey escort: J. Vance. Debt: none."
The Spur sold Finch's maps one sheet at a time. Jory Vance never hired out again; he drives Finch's lead wagon himself now, and doesn't talk about why.
Dustwell's water-sellers were made to stand at the well and hand out cups for a month. Kess never found out who gave her ledger away. She suspected everybody, which suited Sable fine.
Kess got her ledger back and her squeeze went on. Sable was seen once more, on the Saltreach road, and did not wave.
Somewhere in a ditch east of Gantry Yard there is a little circle of ash. Sable visits it, she says, for the view.
Saltreach named its newest well after you. It is the deepest, and the only one that never tastes of salt.
At Gantry Yard there is a picture of you nailed to the crane, and a bounty under it that nobody has collected.
Oskar Vane panned salt by hand for a year in front of the whole of Saltreach. Deputy Renn checked on him every morning, and brought him water, which Oskar said was the cruellest part.
Every family that lost a wagon got an envelope that winter with no name on it. Renn knew whose it was. He never told Ines, and he never told anybody why he was smiling.
Oskar Vane got richer. Renn handed his badge back to Ines the week after, and was seen heading west, towards the Gulch, alone.
Jory Vance kept a second bedroll in Finch's lead wagon for years, "in case the boss turns up." Sometimes you did.
Sable never did settle anywhere. But wherever she went, she left the same mark scratched into a doorframe: two lines, crossed, which she said meant "we were here, and it was fun."
Saltreach made Renn its first sheriff. On his desk he keeps a tin star with a dent in it, and when people ask, he says it belongs to a friend who's still out there walking.
Not everyone who walked beside you finished the walk. They tell their own version of you now, around their own fires.
Odile Brandt stayed mayor of Cinder Gap. Every season she reads the town chest out loud in the Ember Room, to the last chit, and nobody has ever asked her to stop.
Odile Brandt stood down, and Pike ran Cinder Gap for two years, badly. When they asked her back, she said yes on the condition that Pike sweep the street. He did. Badly.
Cinder Gap never learned who sent the last caravan to Mercy. Odile Brandt built a clinic with her own savings the next year, and never said why.
The Reel Kings took their screen tax every season, and Marquee started showing shadow plays on the old screen on summer nights. People came from as far as the Kettle to watch.
The Reel Kings rolled south and were never seen in the Ashwood again. Somebody painted THE END across the drive-in screen. Nobody admits to it.
The Sunset Drive-In stood empty after the shooting. Its screen still catches the last light every evening, showing nothing, to nobody.

Elder Saba walked up the hill to the fire tower with meat and an apology. Ellis Crane still reads the weather into the dark, but now, when he says "visibility to the Ashborn camp is fine", somebody down there waves.
The Ashborn chose a new Ember-Speaker by lot, which Elder Saba said was what the fire would have wanted. No fire has come for the camp since.
Tower Seven fell silent. The next summer a fire started east of the Ashborn camp, upwind, in the spring rain, and there was nobody on the hill to fire a warning.
Doc Sorrel's three fevers all walked out of the clinic. She kept the empty antibiotics case on a shelf, and showed it to anyone who said the old world had nothing left to give.
Pike sold the Mercy antibiotics one tablet at a time. Doc Sorrel never spoke to him again, and treated him last, every time, for the rest of his life.
Dex Reyes took over the Ember Room when Juno married a caravan guard from the Kettle. He still wears the Kings' jacket behind the bar.
Silo 9's purge stayed sealed. Within a year the perch were back at Stillwater's north inlet, and Stillwater barrels were sold from the Kettle to the Ashwood with a little fish painted on the lid.

The coolant poured into the Glass Bowl instead of the reservoir. Stillwater's water ran clear, the pools in the crater glowed brighter every year, and nobody who went down to look at them came back the same.
Silo 9 folded itself into the earth. The Glass Bowl is a lake now, a green one, and nobody drinks from it, and nobody prays to it either.
The Children of the Glass came to Stillwater with their lanterns and nothing else. Sel mends nets now, badly. He never speaks of the Sleeper, but he still faces east when he eats.
Prophet Sel opened the Sleeper's eye and nothing woke. The Children stayed on the rim, fewer every season, until only Brother Amon was left to keep the graves.
Without their Prophet the Children of the Glass scattered across the north. Brother Amon kept his dosimeter, and kept counting, and wrote to anyone who would read it.
Tobiah Fenn kept the Spire's lights on once a month, paid in Stillwater fish. The Duchess called it "a cultural exchange" and never once raised his rent.
With the Duchess gone, the Spire stood empty, and then full of pigeons, and then full of Garage families who liked a view. The Highrisers were never seen again in Old Meridian.
The Garage's generator never failed again. Tobiah Fenn taught three apprentices before he died, and every one of them could open a pre-war padlock with a hairpin.

dustwell.desc: The valley's oldest town, built around a well that is going green. Hard, fair, and running out of time.

saltreach.desc: Salt-traders on the eastern flats. They count everything, share by measure, and turn nobody away.

lamplight.desc: Hooded keepers of the old plant's manuals. They woke the Meridian core on purpose, to light the valley.

gantry.desc: Kess's salvage crews and the guns that guard them. Everything in the yard is for sale, and so is the yard.

haven.desc: Your shelter. Four hundred people behind a steel door, counting cups of water.

spur.desc: The casino in the old motor court. Neutral ground, as long as the house gets its cut.

cinder.desc: A trading town in the basin past Kettle Pass. One street, one saloon, one water tower, and every caravan in the Ashwood stops there.

ashborn.desc: A tribe that came out of the burning forest a generation ago and kept the fire as their god. They trade furs and meat and they do not like towers.

stillwater.desc: Fishers and water-sellers on the valley's last clean reservoir. Slow to trust, quick to feed you.

highrisers.desc: A gang that holds the tallest tower left in Old Meridian and charges rent on the whole skyline.

children.desc: Pilgrims camped on the rim of the bomb crater, who believe something sleeps beneath it and that its light is grace.

opts.t: Everyone wants the core. What does Dustwell want?
I've heard the claims. Here's where I stand.
About the Meridian core. What does Saltreach want?
Everyone's lining up for the core. Tell me again what you want.
Word is you want the regulator.
I have something of yours. A ledger.
Your lead wagon's strongbox. Jory found the wreck.
I have a box of pre-war survey maps.
Ever lose one of Finch's wagons?
The ledger. You wanted to burn it.
Could Saltreach spare a deputy for a while? I could use a rifle.
Someone in Saltreach sold your wagon routes to the Gulch. Here.
This list of wagon routes. It's in your handwriting.
What if we looped the coolant around the cracked housing?
Those symptoms aren't radiation. Grey gums, tremors: that's lead from the old pipes.
Your antenna's impedance is wrong for that cable. Swap the matching coil.

finch_strongbox.desc: A dented steel box from Finch's lead wagon. Inside: survey maps drawn before the war, wrapped in oilcloth.

kess_ledger.desc: Every name in Dustwell who sold Kess water on the side, and what she means to charge per cup when the wells fail.

council_token.desc: Sheriff Voss pinned it on you after the council. It means you speak for nobody but yourself, which is rarer than it sounds.

route_list.desc: Saltreach's salt-wagon routes and times for the month, copied out in a neat merchant's hand. Found on Mags Coyle.

deputy_star.desc: Renn's spare deputy's badge, a salt-crusted tin star. He says you earned it more than he did.

caravan_log.desc: Hester Vail's trail book. The last entries: "Kings took the brahmin at the drive-in turn. Paid the screen tax. Pressing on to Mercy per O.B. Nobody is to know."

mercy_ledger.desc: The hospital pharmacy's stock book, kept to the last week before the war. Half of it is still on the shelves, if you count what the ghouls left.

mercy_meds.desc: Sealed pre-war antibiotics, a whole case, from the Mercy General pharmacy. Doc Sorrel would trade a kidney for this. So would Pike.

crane_radio.desc: A battered forestry-service radio, hand-cranked, with "CRANE" scratched into the case. The Ashborn call it the Burning Man's voice.

fire_log.desc: Ellis Crane's logbook: every smoke he's seen from the tower in eleven years, with times and bearings. Twice, flares fired over the Ashborn camp an hour before the fire reached it.

tull_flint.desc: Found in the hollow under the Ember Mother: rags soaked in lamp oil, a striker, and a pouch of the red ochre only the Ember-Speaker wears.

ember_charm.desc: A twist of charred pine and red thread the Ashborn give to people the fire has decided not to eat. Elder Saba tied it on you herself.

screen_ticket.desc: ADMIT ONE. SUNSET DRIVE-IN. Marquee hands these out to people he's decided not to shoot.

slag_sample.desc: Green-black sludge scooped from the reservoir's north inlet. It glows faintly in the dark and makes the jar warm. The broken pipe above it was stamped SILO 9 COOLANT.

silo_key.desc: A steel key on a beaded chain, pulled from the chassis of the guard robot the Children call the Iron Angel. The tag reads SILO 9 - CREW B - TWO-MAN RULE.

dosimeter_log.desc: Three months of readings from the Children's camp and the crater floor, written up in a careful hand. At the bottom: the names of eleven pilgrims, and the dates they died.

duchess_token.desc: A brass washer stamped with a crown. In Old Meridian it means you've paid, or that the Duchess wants people to think so.

glass_shard.desc: A palm-sized shard of the green glass the bomb made of the crater floor. The Children wear them. It ticks on a counter.

council.desc: Word of the keycard has spread. Everyone with a stake in the valley wants the Meridian core run their way, and Sheriff Voss wants to know whose side you're on before anybody starts shooting.

value.cooked: Hear each claim on the core: Sheriff Voss in Dustwell, Ines in Saltreach, Ro at the Burned Chapel, Kess at Gantry Yard and the Overseer on your wrist radio (

stages.txt: Tell Sheriff Voss in Dustwell whose side you're on.

jory_wagon.desc: Two years ago Vulture Jack's crew took Finch's lead wagon on the western road, and Jory was the guard who lived. The strongbox never turned up.

stages.txt: Find the wreck of Finch's lead wagon on the western road, past the Burned Chapel, and recover the strongbox.
Return the strongbox to Odalys Finch at the Dry Overpass, or sell the maps inside to Madame Vex at the Silver Spur.

sable_ledger.desc: Sable ran with Kess for six years. She left with a grudge and a secret: Kess keeps a ledger of everyone in Dustwell who has been selling her water.

stages.txt: Take Kess's ledger from her stash in Gantry Yard.
Decide what happens to the ledger: Sheriff Voss, Kess herself, or Sable's lighter.

old_colours.desc: Mags Coyle of Rattlesnake Gulch has put a price on Renn's head for deserting. Her crew is camped in the dry wash below the Gulch, waiting on the salt wagons.

stages.txt: Deal with Mags Coyle's crew in the dry wash south-east of Rattlesnake Gulch.
Search Coyle's camp.
Somebody in Saltreach sold Coyle the wagon routes. Talk it over with Renn.
Decide what happens to Oskar Vane: take the routes to Mayor Ines, or have it out with Oskar yourself.

mercy_road.desc: Cinder Gap lives on its caravans, and three of them have gone down the Mercy Falls road this season and not come back. Mayor Brandt wants to know why, and wants it fixed.

stages.txt: Find the last caravan. The Mercy road runs south-east from Cinder Gap.
The log says the Reel Kings at the Sunset Drive-In took a toll. Deal with Marquee: buy the road, run them off, or end them.
The last wagons went on to Mercy Falls "per O.B." Find out what happened at the hospital.
Clear the hospital so Hester Vail can get out.
Tell Mayor Brandt what happened at Mercy Falls, and decide whether Cinder Gap hears about her orders.

burning_man.desc: The Ashborn's Ember-Speaker says the man in the fire tower calls the fires down on the forest. Elder Saba isn't sure, and would rather you looked before her hunters do.

stages.txt: Go to the fire tower in the Ashwood and see the "Burning Man" for yourself.

consequent.value: Bring Elder Saba proof: Crane's fire log, his radio, or whatever is hidden under the Ember Mother.

alternate.value: Bring Elder Saba proof one way or the other: Crane's fire log, or his radio.

stages.txt: Put what you found before Elder Saba.

mercy_ledger.desc: Doc Sorrel has three fevers in the back room and nothing to treat them with. The Mercy General pharmacy was the best-stocked in the county before the war.

stages.txt: Search the pharmacy at Mercy General, on the plateau south-east of Cinder Gap.
Bring the antibiotics to Doc Sorrel. (Pike would pay for them too.)

last_call.desc: Juno's little brother Dex ran off to the Reel Kings at the drive-in. She wants him home before somebody decides to clear the Kings out.

stages.txt: Find Dex Reyes at the Sunset Drive-In and talk him into coming home.
Tell Juno.

still_waters.desc: Stillwater's reservoir is the cleanest water left in the valley, and its fish have started floating belly-up at the north end. Nell Okafor wants to know why before the water sellers in the south find out.

stages.txt: Find out what's coming into the reservoir at its north inlet.
The pipe is stamped SILO 9 COOLANT. The man who knew that silo, Tobiah Fenn, is a prisoner of the Highrisers in the Spire, Old Meridian. Talk to him.

consequent.value: Go down into the Glass Bowl and stop the purge at Silo 9's console.

alternate.value: Silo 9 sits at the bottom of the Glass Bowl. You need a launch key (the guard robot carries one) or Tobiah's override codes to touch its console.

stages.txt: Tell Nell what you did at Silo 9.

the_spire.desc: The Highrisers took Tobiah Fenn, the Garage's engineer, for ransom. Velma Cruz can't pay it and won't forget it.

stages.txt: Get Tobiah Fenn out of the Highrisers' cage in the Spire.
Let Velma know Tobiah is out.

children_of_glass.desc: Brother Amon believes the Prophet is leading the Children of the Glass to their deaths. He wants someone from outside to listen to Sel, and then to decide.

stages.txt: Hear the Prophet out, at the shrine on the Bowl's rim.
Decide what happens to the Children: help Sel open Silo 9, or turn the Children away from it.
Tell Brother Amon.

council_haven.t:
> PRIORITY SIGNAL — WRIST UNIT 12-0447

I am told the people up there are holding a meeting about our regulator.

Let me be plain, so you can repeat it. Haven 12 does not want the reactor. We do not want their water or their power. We want one part, which keeps four hundred people breathing, and then we want to be left alone.

I can't make you choose us. I'm asking you to remember who raised you.

> END

crane_watch.t:
> CRANE, E. — TOWER SEVEN — ASHWOOD DISTRICT

Fire watch, evening report. Wind west-north-west, light. Humidity good. No smoke on any bearing.

Visibility to the Kettle is fine. Visibility to the Ashborn camp is fine. Somebody down there has a cookfire going with too much green wood in it; I can smell it from here.

The forest is asleep. I'm not. This is Tower Seven, signing off, same time tomorrow, same as always.

> END

glass_sermon.t:
> PROPHET SEL — THE RIM OF GRACE

Pilgrims. Listen. Under the glass, the Sleeper dreams.

The old world built it to burn the world, and it would not. It lay down in the dark and made the ground around it into glass, so that we could see our faces in it.

Come to the rim. Bring nothing. Leave your counters and your fears in the valley. The light in the pools is not poison. It is attention.

One day soon its eye will open. Be here when it does.

> END

arguments.value: Word reaches Jory about the maps. He's gone back to Finch's camp, and he won't be coming with you again.
You'd know that neat merchant's hand anywhere in Saltreach: Oskar Vane.
Cinder Gap. The mayor's office is the board building with TOWN HALL on it.
Dex didn't go south with the Kings. Word is he turned up at the Ember Room.
Tobiah, on his way out: "Silo 9 override: seven-four-nine-alpha. Seal the purge. Not the vents. The SEAL."
With the Duchess dead, Tobiah works the chain loose himself.

idle: Ines says I can keep the badge if I stop polishing it.
Lizard tastes better when nobody's hunting you.
I used to watch this road from the other side.
You ever owe somebody your whole life? It's heavy. Good heavy.
barks.leave: I left the Gulch to get away from people like you. I'm going home.
